study_identification.title: Effects of anterior temporal lobe resection on cortical morphology

study_characteristics.study_objective: Quantify how anterior temporal lobe resection (ATLR) affects cortical morphology using traditional measures (thickness, total and exposed surface area) and independent measures (K, I, S), accounting for age/sex/scanner effects via a normative model.

dataset_name.reason: Controls comprise 833 NKI-Rockland participants plus 91 site-specific controls acquired at NHNN/Chalfont under two scanning protocols.
dataset_name.supporting_text: The remaining 833 controls are subjects from the Nathan Kline Institute (NKI) data set... 91 of which were taken together with patients... 22 were taken with scanning protocol 1 and 69 with scanning protocol 2 at the NHNN.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Surface-based paired comparison of pre- vs post-surgery measures with SurfStat (RFT, Cohen's f^2), plus vertex-wise models testing covariates (age at surgery, duration since first seizure, resection volume, side of resection, time to postoperative scan, seizure outcome). No significant covariate effects at cluster p≤.05.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: ATLR induces widespread cortical morphology changes ipsilaterally (orbitofrontal/inferior frontal, pre/postcentral, supramarginal, lingual, lateral occipital) and contralaterally (lateral occipital, inferior frontal/frontal pole), with complementary patterns across traditional and independent measures (K, I, S).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Ipsilateral: increased total and exposed surface area and increased I and S with decreased K in orbitofrontal/inferior frontal gyri; increased K in pre-/postcentral and supramarginal gyri; decreased T and I in lingual and lateral occipital cortex; increased T in precentral gyrus. Contralateral: increased T, At, and I in lateral occipital cortex; increased K in lateral occipital cortex and frontal pole; increased At and I in inferior frontal gyrus. Effect sizes summarized in Supplementary Table 1; results significant at cluster-wise p≤.05 with Cohen's f^2 reported.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: No significant associations between morphological changes and clinical covariates (age at surgery, duration, resection volume, time to scan, seizure outcome); patient age range limited to 19–60 years; language lateralization not analyzed; potential local effects (e.g., frontal lobe 'sagging') may reflect mechanical changes; normative model trained with unmatched NKI protocol data, relying on random-effect adjustment.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Introduces independent morphological measures (K, I, S) at vertex-level patches; uses GAMM-based normative debiasing (age/sex/protocol) and SurfStat RFT for surface statistics; separate ipsi-/contralateral corrections leveraging control data processed with/without temporal lobes.

general_notes.general_notes: Controls: 924 total (833 NKI-Rockland; 91 NHNN site controls [22 protocol 1; 69 protocol 2]); excluded 96 NKI for poor quality/motion. Patients scanned under two protocols (0.94×0.94×1.1 mm; 1×1×1 mm). Data availability: Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7957831).
